_meta.description: Curated allowlist of §197 hyphenated noun-noun compounds (сложносоставные существительные) where BOTH halves normatively decline together, e.g. 'в вагоне-ресторане', 'с инженером-строителем'. Fallback for AgrMnCompoundTermErrorHandler's fused-dictionary gate: pymorphy3's strict OpenCorpora dictionary lacks most real hyphenated compounds even when both halves independently decline (audit finding, 2026-07-12) -- word_is_known(head+'-'+token) is False for инженер-строитель, диван-кровать, генерал-майор, словарь-справочник, музей-усадьба and near everything except a handful of dictionary-fused entries like вагон-ресторан/школа-интернат. This lexicon recovers the common cases the fused lookup misses.
_meta.format: pairs: [head_lemma, second_half_lemma], both lowercase, ё folded to е (matches stanza's own lemmatizer output, not pymorphy's normal_form which always uses ё -- see inflector.py е/ё gotcha)
_meta.scope: ONLY both-halves-decline compounds belong here. Deliberately EXCLUDED: first-half-frozen compounds where only the second part inflects by convention (царь-пушка -> у царь-пушки; плащ-палатка -> в плащ-палатке; military rank compounds генерал-майор/генерал-лейтенант/контр-адмирал -> у генерал-майора, генерал stays Nom; премьер-министр -> к премьер-министру, премьер stays Nom) -- corrupting these would 'fix' an already-frozen first half into a false error. Also excluded: compounds whose first half is grammatically indeclinable regardless of case (кафе-мороженое -- кафе never changes surface form), and plural-only-noun compounds (часы-будильник, юбка-брюки) which the handler's Number logic was not designed against.
_meta.verification: each pair hand-checked for oblique-case agreement on both halves (e.g. Loc 'в кресле-качалке', Ins 'с инженером-строителем', Dat 'к счету-фактуре') and cross-checked that both lemmas are pymorphy3-known, non-Fixd words (loader sanity test enforces this at load time)
_meta.source: manual curation against Rozental grammar tradition (§197 сложносоставные наименования) and standard Russian compound-noun reference lists
